entities.summary:
Íñigo Melchor Fernández de Velasco, 7th Duke of Frías, was a Spanish nobleman and Governor-General of the Spanish Netherlands from 1656 to 1679. He played a key role in the administration of the Dutch Republic's colonies in the Americas and the Caribbean. His tenure was marked by the Dutch Revolt and the subsequent conflicts with the Spanish Empire.

Fernández de Velasco was born on April 16, 1629, in Madrid, Spain, and died on September 29, 1696. He was a member of the powerful Velasco family and held various titles, including Marquess of Frías and Count of Frías.

His legacy as Governor-General is still studied by historians today, who note his efforts to maintain the Dutch Republic's colonies in the face of Spanish aggression. Fernández de Velasco's leadership during this tumultuous period had significant consequences for the development of the Americas.
